Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants and learned A.G.A. for the State.

2. This application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. has been preferred against the order dated 13.10.2022, passed by
the Additional District & Session Judge/Fast Track Court, Moradabad in S.T. No.805 of 2016 (State
Vs. Musheer & others), arising out of Case Crime No.291 of 2015, under Sections 498A, 323, 376,
377 Ipc and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, P.S.- Chhajlet, District- Moradabad,

sentences.text:
whereby non-bailable
warrants have been issued against the applicant.
3.

It has been submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is mother-in-law of opposite party no.2 and she was facing trial in the aforesaid case since the year 2015 but on 13.10.2022 she has fallen ill, due to which she could not appear before the trial Court.

It was pointed Shamima Khatun vs State Of U.P. And Another on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66557200/
1 out that even now the applicant is suffering from liver and kidney related illness and she is lying admitted in Unique Hospital, Chandpur Road, Noorpur, Bijnor.

entities.text: Shamima Khatun vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was submitted that applicant is willing to appear before the trial Court and in view of medical condition of applicant, some interim relief shall be granted to the applicant.
4. Learned A.G.A. has opposed the application.

5. Considering the facts of the matter and submissions of the parties, it is directed that in case applicant appears/ surrenders before the court concerned within a period of six weeks from today and apply for bail/cancellation of warrant, her application shall be considered and decided expeditiously, in accordance with settled law and considering medical condition of the applicant.

It is further directed that for a period of six weeks from today or till the applicant appears/ surrenders before the court concerned, whichever is earlier, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicant in the aforesaid case.
6. With the aforesaid observations, the instant application is finally disposed of.
